payload.goal: Stop sofar disowning its own statusline: refreshInterval is the documented fix for a frozen idle line (Claude Code re-runs the command only on session start / new message / compact / mode toggle), but adding it makes isSofarStatusline's exact-2-key test fail, so install reports 'kept' and uninstall reports 'foreign' on sofar's own entry. Ship refreshInterval in the installed entry and widen the identity test to tolerate that one tunable key, keeping the theirs-wins law for genuinely foreign lines and keeping legacy 2-key installs removable.

payload.because: The two halves were in direct contradiction. refreshInterval is Claude Code's own documented cure for a frozen idle line — the host re-runs a statusLine command only on session start, new assistant message, compact and mode toggles — but under exact-key-count identity, setting it turned sofar's own entry foreign: --uninstall refused to remove it and --install refused to touch it, both telling the user to hand-edit. So the prescribed fix silently broke the uninstall path, reproduced live against 0.23.0. Shipping the key by default removes the discovery burden entirely; widening identity keeps the theirs-wins law intact where it matters (a different command is still someone else's) while an allowlist rather than a blanket accept means an unfamiliar key still counts as customization we must not delete.
payload.chose: D1: statusline identity is type + command, tolerating exactly one tunable key (refreshInterval), and the installed entry ships refreshInterval: 10. isSofarStatusline matches on type + command and requires every remaining key to be in an owned set {type, command, refreshInterval}; any other extra key (e.g. padding) is still foreign. This recognizes both the legacy two-key entry installed before the key shipped and a user-retuned interval.
payload.over: Keeping byte-for-byte identity (Object.keys(v).length === 2) and documenting refreshInterval as a manual edit users make at their own risk; or accepting any object whose command is ours regardless of extra keys.
payload.rule: statusLine identity is type + command plus the owned-key allowlist — never reintroduce an exact key-count test, and add a key to STATUSLINE_OWN_KEYS only when sofar itself writes it.
